summary.intent: Win the Lio 'Keep the Line Running' hackathon challenge for Soony by analyzing the confidential data drops and building a general recheck-and-act agent product (poller, extraction, recompute, act, approval) with a demo and hand-in by Sunday 12:00.
summary.outcome: Found the plan-versus-reality gaps (art books overbooked by 72,000, failed statue lot, game cards short, sleeve revision conflict), built and deployed the Today/Launch app with routines, an approval loop, a demo instance and a README, and fixed many UI bugs; the hand-in demo script, pitch and push of the latest commits remain.

repo: Confidential portal data lives in the gitignored data/ folder and .env; only .env.example is committed. Never put data values in code.

The portal API has only files list, single file and archive.zip, with no notifications or webhooks. Files change without warning, including replacement under the same name, so the poller must compare SHA-256 checksums and keep versions.
Teammates use a CLAUDE.md and PROGRESS.md workflow, so claim work in PROGRESS.md before building.
Entire hooks only write a checkpoint when repo files change; a session with no file changes logs 'skipping checkpoint'.
The live instance sends real supplier emails; a separate demo instance (scripts/demo.sh reset|snapshot|stop) records mail in a dry outbox and runs on its own hostname via the Cloudflare tunnel.
The approval loop is activated by ASK_SIGNOFF_SIMULATE=<seconds>, which simulates Maren's approval; it is off by default and always labeled as simulated.
Push notifications go to every subscribed device, with no per-person targeting. ASK_TEAMS_WEBHOOK is empty, so nothing goes to Teams.
workflow: Check for teammate edits to a shared doc before updating it, and use the doc tools' guide for section replacement.
Run long builds in parallel subagents while writing docs, then commit and restart the server before declaring work live.
Verify UI fixes in the browser with screenshots or scripted key presses (e.g. pressing J repeatedly to check the highlighted row).
Pointing a new hostname at the wrong Cloudflare tunnel causes Error 1033 until the DNS record is corrected.

friction: The portal token was initially empty, so the API returned 401 and the data step was blocked.
The mailbox sync wrote back an old copy of the action log and lost the art book approval record. The email had gone out, but the record vanished, and it was restored from the Sent folder.
Prepared routine steps went stale after the user had already sent the same questions by hand, so 'Do all 4' failed with 'not an open card'.
Two identical routines produced duplicate steps.
Internal messages and escalations were only recorded and reached no one, yet the screen claimed 'DC site lead has it now'.
A routine option bug (a literal 'make po,rev' search) meant nothing was sent.
Routines showed 'not run yet' after being switched on.
A first attempt at the demo DNS record pointed to the wrong tunnel, giving Cloudflare Error 1033.
J/K navigation went through folded cases one by one, so the highlight vanished and the order seemed to jump.
Vague copy such as 'Your agents are on it' and a top bar saying 'nothing needs you' while steps were waiting misled the user.
PackRight received repeated rev C requests after saying it needed documents first.
open_items: Push the unpushed commits (dry mail, demo script, favicon, J/K, wording fixes, label gap).
Write the 3-minute demo script and pitch outline, and record the video, for the 12:00 hand-in.
Build a 'What still saves it' section on Launch (latest arrival per blocker, about 900 Collector's copies saved per hour of earlier arrival).
Delete the duplicate 'Ask Hamburg to count book stock' routine on live.
Set up a Teams webhook (ASK_TEAMS_WEBHOOK) and per-person push routing.
For Maren's view, the top bar still counts Felix's list and says 'nothing needs you'.
Prepare the Felix office-hours question about who moves container NHSU4471921 from the terminal to the DC today.
Send PackRight the rev C file and change notice instead of another identical email.
Register sender addresses in the portal, and ask the Lio engineers whether data is identical across teams.
The shared portal login ended up in Discord history, so change the password after the hack.
